Philosopher Edward Slingerland makes the case for intoxication on episode 1663 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Slingerland wrote a book arguing that alcohol and other drugs helped humans form trust, spark ideas, and build large societies. It is a defense of getting drunk, from a scholar.

He walks Rogan through the evidence, from ancient brewing to lab studies on creativity and bonding. Rogan, no enemy of a good time, asks where the line sits between social glue and harm. The episode is a witty, learned talk that gives an old human habit a surprising job description.
podcast-tuckercarlson-Ks0l_Zpt1xA:
Economist Jeffrey Sachs joins Tucker Carlson to warn against war with Iran. Sachs has advised governments and the United Nations for decades. He links recent events in Syria to a long regional plan.

Sachs argues that Israel's leader has sought to remake the Middle East for thirty years. He calls the result a disaster for the region and for America. He also accuses the Biden team of blocking a smoother change in power. The episode gives a blunt anti-war case from a scholar who favors talks over strikes. His tone is urgent, even when the talk turns technical.
